title: Contact count gave no prediction gain after shared calibration in 35 inputs to one leech motor neuron
abstract: We tested whether contact count improved cross-trial complex coherence prediction after a common gain, phase and offset map. Anatomy and voltage imaging came from the same leech ganglion. In 35 mapped inputs with at least two contacts, a map with log count and its source-value interaction increased held-out mean squared error by 8.0% in two swim trials and 6.9% in three left-bend trials. All eight directed transfers had more error. Count-label references gave Holm p = 0.7984 for both behaviors. All mapped inputs, strict confidence and removal of the largest count also gave no gain. Fixed-loss input resampling left small gains possible and is not an animal-level interval. One animal, few trials, model variance, uncertain matches and absent spectral errors limit inference. The result limits this model, not the functional role of count. Code, aggregate results, figures, hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.
